text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Deaths from drug taking in 1996 in Germany climb for the first time in five years to 1,712, a rise of 9.4 percent.
- New U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright visits Bonn as part of her first foreign tour since taking office in January and speaks of "deep friendship" with Germany.
- More than 20,000 postal workers demonstrate against the planned end to the century-old monopoly of the post office.
- Labour Minister Norbert Bluem says planned pensions and tax reforms must be negotiated together.
- Opposition Social Democrat (SPD) party manager Franz Muenterering says he sees a chance of reaching agreement with the ruling coalition when the two sides meet to discuss planned tax reforms.
HANDELSBLATT
- Germany and the United States are firmly decided they want to push through the eastward expansion of NATO at the Madrid summit in July.
- Dollar climbs above 1.70 marks.
- A day before decisive coalition talks on the planned ending of the German post office monopoly, over 20,000 postal workers protest in Bonn.
- German engineering group Kloeckner Werke AG said it has turned its business fortunes around after 20 years of crisis.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Drug deaths rise in 1996 to 1,712 for the first time since 1991, with use of so-called "designer drugs" climbing sharply.
- Visit of Albright to Bonn used to show harmony between two countries.
- Protesting postal workers fear for their jobs.
DIE WELT
- Germany and the United States in agreement over the eastward expansion of NATO after Albright visit.
- Deaths from drugs in Germany climb for the first time since 1991.
- Labour Minister Bluem wants talks with opposition SPD on reform of pensions insurance.
- SPD lays down position on tax reform ahead of talks with ruling coalition next week.
- Postal workers protest against plans to end post office monopoly.
